questions.problem: Given the polynomial $P(x)=(x+2)^{2}(1-x),$ find the solution of $P(x)<0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)<0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies below the $x$-axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)=(x+2)^{2}(1-x)$ are $x=-2$ and $x=1,$ where

- $x=-2$ has multiplicity $2,$ and

- $x=1$ is a simple root.

Also, $P(x)$ is a cubic polynomial with a negative leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/9380e0f00b0df89a4148aa184ad73a1edfad8b76c9755f23926d6b856fdddb62.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)<0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is below the $x$-axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (1,\infty ).$

questions.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $f(x)\le 0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=f(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis or touches this axis.

First, we factor the polynomial $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}-3x+2) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}-x-2x+2) \\  & ={x}^{2}[(x(x-1)-2(x-1)] \\  & ={x}^{2}(x-1)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

The roots of the polynomial are $x=0$, $x=1$ and $x=2,$ where

- $x=0$ has multiplicity $2,$ and

- $x=1$ and $x=2$ are simple roots.

So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/baf599e732aa524409881d4bc7598c3f998cffe116ca1cdcd76fb6e6bd49a078.png)

Since we are interested in solving $f(x)\le 0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is

$$
x\in {0}⋃[1,2].
$$
